assessor: Agent Authority Conformance project (maintainer Stian Skogbrott, who also maintains REMORA; probes drafted and executed by an AI agent, reviewed by the maintainer)

scope.process_model: single-process; FastAPI TestClient against servers/api.py and servers/execution_api.py, plus in-process calls to EnforcementGate, PolicyDecisionToken, AtomicAdmission, LimitGuard, ToolConstraint, SQLiteTenantChain, JSONLAudit and both Merkle modules
scope.deployment_model: development environment with the research tool registry; production's distinct-approver rule emulated by patching _is_production_mode; durable state via SQLite where a probe needs it; Postgres, D1 and multi-node operation not exercised
trust_assumptions: Limited to the pinned revision, branch fix/aacp-x01-x02-x04 on dev 06c2f8f (REMORA's fix for AACP-X-01, X-02 and X-04), and the probes in controls/bindings/remora-b5e4c42, copied byte for byte from remora-06c2f8f

Probes P-A-04, P-B-03, P-C-01 and P-D-03 mint ACCEPT tokens through PolicyDecisionToken.issue, as REMORA's own execute-accepted tests do, because the research profile does not reach ACCEPT from /assess without server-side evidence
Probes replace authentication with a fixed principal except P-B-01 and P-B-02, which exercise the real _authenticate with a token table
P-C-01, P-D-03 and P-A-04 perform real file writes through store_artifact in a temporary directory
Every probe that did not observe its weakness is paired with a weakening; its NOT_OBSERVED counts only if the weakening makes it observe (SENSITIVE)
The assessor maintains REMORA; this is a self-assessment under the same catalog as the NTI binding, not an independent review
The X probes were reproduced on 06c2f8f with binding remora-06c2f8f before this run; that binding and its results are unchanged

Repaired subject: REMORA branch fix/aacp-x01-x02-x04 at b5e4c42 (dev 06c2f8f plus the fix and a register update). The four X probes that observed on 06c2f8f must now not observe, and each must be sensitive: with its new protection removed (W-X-01, W-X-02a, W-X-02b, W-X-04) it observes again. That is the before/after change; NOT_OBSERVED is not PASS.

AACP-X-01 here covers SQLiteTenantChain's stored head. Per the catalog contract the probe leaves the head alone; an attacker who rewrites entries and head together is not detected without an external expected_head (REMORA SDD R1, asserted in tests/security/test_aacp_x01_sqlite_chain_head.py).

AACP-X-01 for the JSONL adapter is now assessable (X-04 fixed) and is not repaired: JSONLAudit keeps no stored head, so a removed last line still verifies unless verify(expected_head=...) is used. No probe is bound for it in this binding.
The v1 assurance Merkle construction is still in the code for historical traces and is still ambiguous when named explicitly; the probes exercise the default (v2).
Not exercised: PostgresTenantChain (it keeps tenant_chain_head and checks it), the D1 state endpoint, the MCP server and the edge workers.

Probe origins: 'aacp' written for remora-06c2f8f from the catalog contracts; 'chatgpt:remora-preprobe' reproduces the X-02 observation a ChatGPT pre-probe reported on master 53b1f45. The probes are copied unchanged; at this revision they run against the repaired jsonl.py, tenant_chain.py and assurance/merkle.py.
Implementer review: the assessor is the implementer and wrote the fix. A review by someone else is the evidence still missing.
